budget_pairing_note: tau_b = measured latency of P2.1's own BOPs-selected plan at budget b (NOT fraction x Latency_id -- that pairing made 5/6 budgets mathematically infeasible, a confound from BOPs cost's much wider achievable dynamic range than real latency's, not a hardware-reality finding -- see README.md's Budget pairing section). Guarantees feasibility by construction.
bits_to_precision_note: bits=8 and bits=6 both execute at measured INT8 engine latency (BEST ACHIEVABLE, explicit Q/DQ -- see jetson-orinnx/README.md's INT8 findings) -- there is no distinct hardware datapath per bit count on this device. See this file's module docstring.
joint_staged_note: CORRECTED on review, 2026-07 -- do NOT read n_joint_staged_collapsed as a re-test of experiments/phase1_E1-E5_E4a/E5_allocator_G1.py's 'staging collapse' finding. At this run's 6 budgets (paired to P2.1's own BOPs-selected plans' measured latency -- see 'Budget pairing'), tau_b >= Latency_id at n_degenerate_budgets of them -- looser than doing nothing, so the identity plan is trivially optimal for every selection rule there, a degenerate coincidence, not a genuine joint-vs-staged test. Joint vs staged under real hardware cost remains UNTESTED until a budget sweep set directly INSIDE the achievable range (min_achievable_fraction_of_identity above 1.0, i.e. compression genuinely forced) is run -- see jetson-orinnx/README.md's 'Joint vs staged' section for the planned follow-up.
